question: A coat is 40% off, with an extra 25% off at the till. What is the total discount, in percent?
answer: 55%, not 65%: the second discount comes off an already reduced price.
move: Discounts taken one after another multiply; they never simply add up.
ask: Which deal with stacked discounts have I added up instead of multiplying?
hint: Turn each discount into the share you still pay, then multiply.
steps: After 40% off you pay 0.60 of the price.
source: Chen and Rao, When two plus two is not equal to four, Journal of Consumer Research, 2007
quote: Sequential percentage discounts generate more purchasers, sales, revenue, and profit than the economically equivalent single percentage discount.
